cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make Help Define Us
cards.instruction: Get their help, then use how it is offered to redefine what the relationship means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Check the spelling in my complaint. Leave the angry sentence exactly where I've put it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a good sentence. I only wanted to fix one word.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're my collaborator, not my minder. Fix the word and put your name beside mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like the sentence, but I don't want my name on the complaint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keep yours off. We'll call you my editor, and I'll take the blame. You can tell people you tried to restrain me.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assigns limited editing; A3 turns B praise into collaborator status and orders signature; A5 grants a narrower editor role when B refuses public ownership.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 precise correction and praise; A5 uses B4 signature refusal to separate editing from responsibility.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers real help and B4 maintains a reasonable boundary without withdrawing it.

heightening.evidence: A5 redefines the relationship again because B4 rejects co-authorship, while A retains authority to name roles and grant an account of events.

specificity.evidence: A1 complaint editing, word correction and signature make the stakes concrete without requiring complaint content.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 taking blame and licensing the restraint story is compact, characterful generosity rather than a detached gag.
